title: Six Months in Hildesheim: More Than Just an Erasmus 🇩🇪
description: New places, international friendships, unexpected challenges, and everything I learned from stepping outside my comfort zone.
paragraphs: When I left Italy for my Erasmus semester in Hildesheim, Germany, I honestly had no idea what to expect.
All I knew was that I was excited. Excited about moving to a new country, experiencing a different culture, and stepping away from everything I was familiar with.
Of course, I had my worries too.
The biggest one? The language barrier.
I had never studied German before, and even though I could speak English, I kept underestimating my own abilities.

I still remember one of my first meetings with my academic coordinator at the University of Hildesheim. For the first time, I had to explain my academic background, discuss my course choices, and talk about my studies entirely in English with a German university professor.
It might sound like a small thing, but for me, it was a big deal.
Everything felt new, challenging, and incredibly exciting at the same time.
And that was just the beginning.

sections.heading: From Strangers to Friends
paragraphs: One of the things that surprised me the most was how quickly an unfamiliar place started to feel like home.

Within just a few weeks, I had already found my first group of international friends. People from different countries, speaking different languages, with different cultures and backgrounds, but all sharing the same desire to explore, connect, and make the most of this adventure.
There's one little detail that still makes me smile.
After spending entire days speaking English, I would return to my room and call my parents or friends back in Italy. And somehow, speaking Italian again felt strangely unusual!
It was a funny feeling, but also a sign that, without even realizing it, I was adapting to a completely new everyday life.

sections.heading: One Train Ticket, Endless Adventures 🚆
paragraphs: If there's one thing I absolutely loved about being a student in Germany, it was the opportunity to travel.
Thanks to the Semesterticket, which gave me access to regional trains across Germany, almost every weekend could turn into a new adventure.
Together with my friends, I explored Hannover, Bremen, Hamburg, Lübeck, Berlin, Dresden, and many other places.
Every trip was an opportunity to discover a new city, wander through unfamiliar streets, try local food, and, most importantly, create memories together.
And then December arrived.
I simply cannot talk about my Erasmus in Germany without mentioning the Christmas markets.
The beautiful lights, the festive atmosphere, the smell of warm Glühwein, Bratwurst, Currywurst, Lebkuchen, Zimtsterne, and so many other delicious things.
I had seen German Christmas markets in pictures before, but experiencing them in person, surrounded by friends, was something else entirely.
Those are the kinds of moments that stay with you.

sections.heading: Learning Beyond the Classroom
paragraphs: Of course, Erasmus wasn't just about travelling and making friends.
Academically, it gave me the chance to experience a different university environment and challenge myself in ways I hadn't expected.
One of the most meaningful experiences was working on a university project with an international team.
At first, I was a little nervous.

I wondered whether communication would be difficult, whether we'd approach problems differently, and whether we could develop the same kind of teamwork that usually comes naturally when working with classmates from your own university.
Well, it turned out to be one of the coolest parts of my Erasmus!
I realized that different backgrounds don't necessarily create barriers. Sometimes, they're exactly what makes collaboration more interesting.
Different perspectives, different approaches, and different ways of solving the same problem.
Working together taught me that there's so much to learn from people who see things differently from you.
And remember my initial fear of not speaking German?
Well, I actually decided to take a German language course alongside my Computer Science classes.
After years of studying programming, algorithms, and other technical subjects, suddenly finding myself learning vocabulary, grammar, and pronunciation again felt almost surreal!
But it was also refreshing.
Being a complete beginner again, making mistakes, and slowly understanding things that initially seemed impossible reminded me how rewarding learning something entirely new can be.

sections.heading: Six Months Later, What Did I Take Home?
paragraphs: Looking back, I realize that some of the most valuable things I learned during those months had nothing to do with university exams or textbooks.
I learned to be more independent, to trust myself more, and to stop letting the fear of not being good enough hold me back.
I discovered that you don't need to speak a language perfectly to build genuine friendships.
I learned that stepping outside your comfort zone can be uncomfortable, but it's often where the best experiences begin.
And most importantly, I met some incredible people with whom I shared moments I'll never forget.
If I could go back in time, I would make the same decision all over again.
Without hesitation.

sections.heading: To Anyone Thinking About Erasmus
paragraphs: If you're a student considering Erasmus but you're worried about delaying your graduation, struggling with the language, or simply being far away from home, there's one thing I'd like to tell you:
Just go for it!
Don't wait until you feel completely ready, because chances are, you never will.
Yes, there will be challenges. You might struggle with an exam, deal with confusing bureaucracy, miss home, or find yourself in situations where you have absolutely no idea what you're doing.
And that's okay. It's all part of the experience.
Erasmus isn't just about passing exams or earning university credits.

It's about the friendships that start with a simple "Where are you from?", the conversations in a language you once thought you couldn't speak well enough, the spontaneous train trips, and all those little moments that somehow end up changing the way you see the world.
I left Italy with a suitcase full of doubts and excitement. I came back with new friendships, more confidence in myself, and a completely different perspective on the world.
And I think that's the greatest gift Erasmus could have given me. 🇪🇺
